messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary below against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement is internally inconsistent, so I would not treat a match decision as settled yet.

“Between 9 and 5 years” reverses the usual order. A range is normally written low-to-high (“between 5 and 9”). Read strictly, no amount of experience is both at least 9 and at most 5, so the stated range is empty and nobody would match. The likely intent is a swap or typo for 5–9 years, but that is an assumption, not what the posting says. Other readings (at least 5, at least 9, exactly those two figures) are also possible and would change the result.

The summary itself is clear on the relevant point: 7 years of backend engineering, with a recent high-volume settlement pipeline. That number only matters once the bounds are fixed.

How should “between 9 and 5” be read: as 5–9 inclusive, as a minimum of 5, as a minimum of 9, or as written (empty range)?
